concept.tagline: Unifying cheap cloud object storage with ACID snapshot isolation, hidden partitioning, and Bronze/Silver/Gold Medallion refinement via Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake.
concept.purpose: Build a progressive mental model of modern Lakehouses—from how Iceberg metadata trees achieve ACID on immutable S3 objects to CoW vs MoR and file compaction.

spark.summary: A Data Lakehouse unifies the low-cost, open-format object storage of a Data Lake with the ACID transactions, schema enforcement, and fast SQL performance of a Data Warehouse—typically organized via Medallion (Bronze, Silver, Gold) layers.
spark.keyTakeaway: Store data once in open table formats (Apache Iceberg or Delta Lake) on cloud object storage, using Bronze/Silver/Gold tiers to progressively refine raw events into governed, query-ready business tables.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** A **Data Lakehouse** places an open transactional metadata layer (**Apache Iceberg**, **Delta Lake**, or **Apache Hudi**) directly over immutable Parquet/ORC files in S3/GCS.

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts How Apache Iceberg Achieves ACID & 99% File Pruning on Immutable S3 (Catalog CAS -> metadata.json -> Manifest List -> Manifest File -> Parquet (128-512MB)); Bronze -> Silver -> Gold Pipeline on Shared Object Storage (Kafka / Debezium -> Bronze Iceberg -> Silver Iceberg -> Gold (Z-Ordered)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Choose CoW vs MoR based on your read/write ratio and CDC `MERGE` frequency. Enforce strict layer boundaries via catalog RBAC: restrict BI service accounts to **Gold** schemas, isolate backfills on Iceberg branches, and enable **Deletion Vectors** (Delta).

**Failure Modes & Application:** Explore real-time lakehouse architectures, CDC ingestion, Spark shuffle skew tuning, and dimensional star schemas.

learningJourney.title: What is a Data Lakehouse & Medallion Architecture
learningJourney.explanation:
A **Data Lakehouse** places an open transactional metadata layer (**Apache Iceberg**, **Delta Lake**, or **Apache Hudi**) directly over immutable Parquet/ORC files in S3/GCS. Object stores lack in-place updates, so Iceberg maintains an atomic `metadata.json` catalog CAS pointer -> `manifest list` -> `manifest files` (with per-file min/max column stats) -> `Parquet data files`.

Data flows through three **Medallion** tiers: **Bronze** (raw append-only history), **Silver** (cleansed, deduplicated, conformed entities via `MERGE INTO`), and **Gold** (Z-ordered business aggregates & ML feature tables).

learningJourney.title: Where a Lakehouse Fits (and Where OLTP / Managed Warehouses Win)
learningJourney.explanation: Lakehouses shine for multi-terabyte unified BI + ML without vendor lock-in, but are the wrong tool for sub-10ms OLTP lookups or tiny <1 TB SQL-only datasets.

learningJourney.title: How to manage Compaction, Z-Ordering & Hidden Partitioning
learningJourney.explanation:
Keep a Lakehouse fast with four automated maintenance jobs:

1. **Bin-Packing Compaction**: Merge streaming 50 KB files into **128–512 MB** Parquet files (`rewrite_data_files`) to prevent planner OOMs.
2. **Z-Ordering / Clustering**: Sort rows inside Parquet by common filter keys (`customer_id`, `tenant_id`) so row-group min/max stats skip 95%+ of blocks.
3. **Snapshot Expiration & Vacuum**: Expire snapshots >7 days and remove orphan files >24h.
4. **Hidden Partitioning**: Use `PARTITIONED BY (days(event_ts))` in Iceberg so queries filtering `WHERE event_ts >= '2026-11-01'` prune partitions automatically.
learningJourney.markdownContent:
```sql
-- Apache Iceberg table with hidden daily partitioning & maintenance procedures (Spark SQL)
CREATE TABLE silver.orders (
    order_id BIGINT,
    customer_id BIGINT,
    status STRING,
    total_cents BIGINT,
    event_ts TIMESTAMP
) USING iceberg
PARTITIONED BY (days(event_ts));

-- Periodic bin-packing compaction + Z-order clustering + snapshot expiration:
CALL system.rewrite_data_files(table => 'silver.orders', strategy => 'sort', sort_order => 'zorder(customer_id)');
CALL system.expire_snapshots(table => 'silver.orders', older_than => TIMESTAMP '2026-11-10 00:00:00');
```

learningJourney.title: Alternatives: Copy-on-Write vs. Merge-on-Read & Warehouse vs. Lake
learningJourney.explanation: Choose CoW vs MoR based on your read/write ratio and CDC `MERGE` frequency.

benefits: Fastest BI read latency—no delete files to merge at query time.
costs: Rewrites entire 256 MB Parquet files even for a single-row update.

benefits: Fast CDC upserts and GDPR deletes via lightweight positional/equality delete files.
costs: Reads slow down if delete files accumulate before background compaction.

benefits: Zero manual compaction or vacuuming; lowest ops burden.
costs: Higher bundled storage/egress costs and tighter engine lock-in.

learningJourney.purpose: The trade-off: compare competing approaches across latency, consistency, and operational cost.

learningJourney.title: Production Architecture: Medallion Governance & File Health
learningJourney.explanation: Enforce strict layer boundaries via catalog RBAC: restrict BI service accounts to **Gold** schemas, isolate backfills on Iceberg branches, and enable **Deletion Vectors** (Delta) or **Puffin NDV sketches** (Iceberg) to accelerate `MERGE` mutations.

ideas.title: Avoid Over-Partitioning
ideas.description: Never partition by `user_id` or `hour + country + device_type`, which creates sparse 200 KB files that destroy Parquet compression and planning speed.

ideas.title: Prevent Catalog Divergence
ideas.description: Never write directly to S3 Parquet paths bypassing the Iceberg REST / Unity Catalog—direct writes create invisible rows and stale metadata.

knowledgeCheck.question: A streaming Flink job commits 1,000 tiny 50 KB Parquet files per hour into an Iceberg table partitioned by `hour + country + device_type`, causing Trino query planners to OOM. What are the two root fixes?

options.text: Use coarser partitioning (e.g., `days(event_ts)`) and schedule periodic `rewrite_data_files` bin-packing compaction to 128–512 MB files
options.feedback: Correct: coarse hidden partitioning + bin-packing compaction eliminates the small-files metadata explosion.

options.text: Switch from Merge-on-Read to Copy-on-Write without changing partitioning
options.feedback: Over-partitioning by `hour + country + device_type` still produces tiny files under CoW.

options.text: Bypass the Iceberg catalog and query S3 Parquet paths directly
options.feedback: Bypassing the catalog breaks ACID snapshot isolation and causes S3 ListObjects bottlenecks.

_recommendedProblem.prompt: Redesign an active-active multi-master relational replication pipeline between us-east-1 and eu-west-1 (6,000 writes/sec, 85 ms WAN RTT, < 15 ms p99 local commit) so a 9-minute transatlantic partition and 180-250 ms NTP clock skew never cause silent Last-Write-Wins (LWW) overwrites.
